Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

advantage noun

a better position than others

also have the advantage, have an advantage over, be at an advantage, edge, upper hand

classical

Caes. BG 7.65: quod hostēs equitātū superiōrēs esse intellegēbat
Cic. Off. 1.90: facilitāte et hūmānitāte … superiōrem fuisse

superior esse

phrase: superior agrees with the subject; the ablative says in what

have the advantage, be better placed (in something)

Latin says who is superior and in what (equitātū, in cavalry; numerō, in numbers) where English speaks of having an advantage. Lewis & Short: “of strength or success in battle or any contest, victorious, conquering, stronger, superior”.

Other words

  • praestō, praestāre, praestitī, praestitum — stand out, have the advantage over, be better than

    verb, first conjugation, with the dative of those surpassed and the ablative of the respect · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.2.2: cum virtūte omnibus praestārent; Cic. Inv. 1.5: quā rē hominēs bēstiīs praestent (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Impersonally, praestat, “it is better” (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Philippum quidem Macedonum rēgem rēbus gestīs et glōriā superātum ā fīliō, facilitāte et hūmānitāte videō superiōrem fuisse

    Philip, king of Macedon, was outdone by his son in achievements and glory, but in good nature and kindness, I see, he had the advantageCic. Off. 1.90

  • Caesar, quod hostēs equitātū superiōrēs esse intellegēbat …

    Caesar, because he saw that the enemy had the advantage in cavalry …Caes. BG 7.65

See also advantage, better, win.
